Subject: Urgent: Spiking 5xx/429s and timeouts — impacting production

Hi Sean / Dev team,

We started seeing a sudden increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API around 08:50 PST. Our ingestion pipeline is timing out and we've got several downstream jobs failing. Error pattern looks like repeated timeouts followed by bursts of 429s (rate limit). This is affecting our real-time analytics dashboard and we have multiple customers reporting delayed data.

Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on your side? We need an ETA and any immediate mitigations you can apply. Attached are a few sample request IDs and timestamps.

Sample request ids: req_9a8b7cde, req_9a8b82f1

Eva — thanks for flagging this and sharing the request ids. We’re treating this as a Sev-1 and have the infra team on it now. Quick summary of immediate actions we’re taking: 

- Spun up additional Dedicated pool nodes for Acme’s tenant (temporary scale)
- Enabled conservative request-level throttling for noisy endpoints to limit retry amplification
- Collated request ids you sent and passed them to engineering for trace analysis
- Opening a page on our status system and will keep it updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260218-acme

Can you confirm whether your clients have aggressive retry logic (no jitter/backoff)? That pattern often amplifies transient throttles into retry storms and spikes 5xxs. If you can temporarily reduce retry rate on the client side it’ll help the overall recovery.

ETA for visible improvement: 30-60 minutes for error rate reduction after scale + throttle. I’ll post an update at +30m.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s — initial findings and mitigation

Team,

Quick update from infra traces:
- Root cause: a sudden client-side retry storm combined with a partially degraded routing worker in one us-west-2 cluster. The worker started returning 503s on large input sequences which triggered client retries; retries caused sustained queue pressure and token timeouts.
- What we did: removed the degraded worker from the pool, scaled the routing tier + autoscaler thresholds, and pushed an emergency kernel patch to avoid the edge-case OOM that was exacerbating timeouts.
- Short-term mitigation we applied (already live):
  * Conservative per-tenant concurrency cap (Acme) to prevent head-of-line blocking
  * Automatic exponential backoff enforcement for retrying clients at the edge (soft-throttle header)
  * Temporary fallback model route (smaller quantized variant) for large sequences to reduce tail latency

Observed impact: error rate dropped from ~12% 5xx/429 at peak to ~1.8% within 20 minutes after scale and caps. We still see bursts when client retries are aggressive.

Next steps:
- Full root cause postmortem + writeup (drafting now)
- Plan to restore normal concurrency thresholds after we confirm sustained stability for 24h
- Schedule configuration change to make the soft-throttle rule configurable by partner stage (so we don’t require manual intervention)

Will follow up with the postmortem draft and timeline for returning to baseline.

- Dev

Subject: Status update: 5xx/429 spike — visible improvement, recommended client changes

Eva — brief status update for your team: 

- What happened: transient routing worker degradation + client retry amplification led to elevated 5xx/429s and timeouts.
- What we did: removed bad worker, scaled routing tier, applied soft-throttle + per-tenant caps, enabled smaller-quant model fallback for large sequences.
- Current state: error rate reduced to ~0.9% 5xx/429 across your traffic. Latency tails improved by ~35%.
- Recommended action for Acme: implement exponential backoff with jitter client-side and reduce retry attempts for requests that return 5xx/429. We can provide a short code snippet you can drop into your retry wrapper if helpful.

We’ll continue to monitor and keep the incident page updated. ETA to normal baseline: 24 hours of steady metrics; I’ll follow up tomorrow morning with a postmortem draft.

Sean
